title: Redline acceptance profiles and dynamic price adjuster for enterprise offers
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Create a combined system of contract redline acceptance profiles (per customer segment and SSQ outcome) and a dynamic price adjuster that automatically suggests a target price uplift to compensate for accepted legal concessions (indemnity/liability/SLA). Integrate suggestions into Sales Quote builder and run as a pricing experiment to measure conversion and margin impact.
problem: Sales currently awaits manual legal review for most redline concessions or uses conservative fixed discounts. This slows deal cycles and reduces win rates; engineering/legal time is overloaded by low-risk exceptions. Pricing experiments lack a closed-loop signal that ties contract concessions to realized margin impact.
goals: 1) Reduce time-to-contract for low/medium risk redlines by 50% for self-serve and early-enterprise customers. 2) Maintain expected margin by applying an automated price uplift calibrated to risk. 3) Surface clear handoffs to Legal for high-risk exceptions.
proposed_solution: Build 'Acceptance Profiles' keyed by customer tier (startup, scale, enterprise), SSQ score bands, and common clause families (indemnity cap, warranty, data-escrow, SLA credits). Each profile encodes which concessions can be auto-approved and a corresponding price uplift matrix. Hook profiles into the Quote Builder so sales sees 'Suggested Concession + Price Delta' inline. Add telemetry for deal outcomes, legal escalations, and realized revenue impact for experiment analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance profiles schema defined and stored in config service
Quote Builder UI surfaces suggested concession and price uplift, editable by rep
Back-end calculates uplift per-line item and shows net ARR impact in quote preview
Auto-approval triggers legal queue only for exceptions outside profile thresholds
Experiment tracks conversion, average uplift captured, and legal review volume
Security sign-off completed for SSQ-to-profile data flow
notes: Profile inputs: SSQ score, customer ARR band, industry vertical, prior incidents
Uplift calculation model initially deterministic: sum of clause risk weights -> % uplift; plan to iterate to ML calibration after N deals
We will surface a human-readable rationale for each suggested concession for auditability
Legal requires retention of original signed clause text and an audit log of auto-approvals
Fallback: when sales manually overrides suggested uplift, capture reason for analysis

risks_and_tradeoffs: Automation reduces cycle time but may increase residual liability if risk weights are miscalibrated
Conservative initial uplift may depress conversion; optimistic initial uplift risks margin leakage
Maintaining auditability requires extra logging and storage costs
SSQ data quality varies by counterparty; we need a normalization layer to avoid bad signals
compliance_and_controls: Audit log exported daily to secure bucket with retention policy
Manual review trail preserved in Legal queue with reason codes
All SSQ fields used are whitelisted and GDPR-reviewed by Privacy
KMS-wrapped keys for any persisted sensitive fields
metrics_and_experiment_plan: Primary metric: contract cycle time (signature lag) change vs control
Secondary metrics: conversion rate, realized price uplift captured (ARR delta), legal review volume
Canary: 2-week run on Startup & Scale cohorts, target sample 120 quotes
Stopping criteria: >10% net margin regression or >20% increase in legal escalations
